summary: PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20 is careful on the mathematics. The 136 items match the published Acta text. The eight library citations hold at the pins. The ten source issues are right, including E2's non-reduced BNR witness and E4's twisting argument. No erratum exists. It breaks on ownership. Item 044 (quasi-nilpotence is nilpotent p-curvature) is routed into CrystallineCohomology:CR.1 but depends on p-curvature and Higgs bundles, which are owned by CR.1's own Part II and by HodgeStructuresPartII, both of which import CR.1. That is a cycle, and it leaves 045–046 marked planned in a form CR.1 does not plan (high). Route 6 goes into the finished GlobalGaloisDeformations blueprint and is never applied, so 091–093 are planned nowhere, while 090 is in fact planned there (high). Faltings's p-adic Simpson correspondence and crystalline local systems duplicate the accepted PadicHodgeTheory Part II of HEUER-25 and GUO-REINECKE-24. The companion relation and Abe's Theorem 4.2.2 duplicate ABE-18's GlobalShtukas Part II. The ℓ-adic weight inputs of Proposition 7.4(2) have no item, although DWP.7 and GS.6 plan most of them (medium). I found two source mistakes the extraction missed: the proof of Lemma 4.11 cites Lemma 3.4 for a fact it does not give (medium), and the proof of Lemma 5.5 concludes a false χ=1 (low). Five slips, a Mathlib Morita equivalence the items overlook, two item inaccuracies and a missing sourceVersions are low. 11 findings: 2 high, 4 medium, 5 low.

Source versions, fetched 30 September 2026. The published Acta PDF (https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/acta/2020/0225/0001/ACTA-2020-0225-0001-a002.pdf) has SHA-256 0d81a6d3…1cfab, which matches the recorded hash. arXiv v4 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.00752v4) has SHA-256 bcc435b5…c4eb. The arXiv API lists v4 (1 June 2020) as the latest version.

Errata search, 30 September 2026. Crossref for doi:10.4310/ACTA.2020.v225.n1.a2 has no update-to, relation or updated-by, and a Crossref query for an erratum finds none. Esnault's publication list (https://page.mi.fu-berlin.de/esnault/helene_publ.html), entry 126, lists no erratum, although the list does link errata for other papers (71b, 95b, 118b, 138b).

The whole published text, pp.103–158, read with pdftotext: §§1–8, Appendix A and the references. Page 139 was rendered as an image to confirm that Theorem 5.4 restricts to π₁(X_{K(s)-bar}) (the bar is printed, so no finding). The arXiv v4 text was compared at every new finding's locator: Lemma 4.11, Lemma 5.5, Corollary 4.17, Lemma 5.9.

All 136 item statements compared with the paper, including the hypotheses of the main theorems. Theorems 1.4, 1.6 and 1.8 need X smooth connected projective over C, (E,∇) stable and rigid with torsion determinant, and a chosen and shrunk model S (convention C). Corollary 4.17 gives motivicity only on a dense open of a curve. Theorem 6.1 gives unitary, not finite, monodromy. Proposition 8.2 has a universal premise. Items 052 (disjoint sections), 058–060 (counts), 063–065, 079–085 (the inverse-limit argument) and 104 were checked step by step against pp.123–137 and 145–146.

Every source issue E1–E10 checked at its locator, with the review's confirmations; I agree with each. E2's witness was checked: (λ³+εω²λ)^p = λ^{3p} over k[ε]/ε², and the zero section lies in Z′_a, while χ_dR(F*O³) = λ³. So were E3's witness (u↦t², t⁸≠0 but u²↦0 on k[t]/t⁴) and E4's twisting argument (χ^r=1 in the p-group 1+m_A forces χ=1 when p∤r).

Missed-mistake hunt. Found E11 (Lemma 4.11), E12 (Lemma 5.5) and five slips (finding 8). Candidates checked and rejected: (a) the count equality n_dR(X)=n_dR(X_s) in §3.3 needs the spread sections to stay distinct at s. That is a shrinking the paper leaves implicit, but item 052 already imposes it. (b) Proposition 7.4(2) invokes generic base change [Ka1, 8.0] after s is fixed. This is harmless: the crystalline–de Rham comparison on the W(k(s))-lift holds at every s. (c) Irreducibility of the isocrystal M_s on C_s in Corollary 4.17 follows from absolute irreducibility of (E,∇)|_C over K(s) and rigid GAGA. (d) Example 6.3 needs no unit hypothesis (finding 10).

Packets read: CrystallineCohomology--CR.0 (partial, nodes only in CR.0 and CR.4), GlobalGaloisDeformations (done; R04.1–R04.2 nodes, finding 2) and PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology (304 nodes). Routes. All four Part II parents exist, and their atlas titles match the corrected route titles exactly. No accepted restructuring (RS-01…RS-33) extends any of the four parents, so there is no Part II/Part III collision. make_queue.paper_designs merges all Part II proposals of one parent into one design job, so the sibling proposals (DegeneratingHodgeStructures, BrauerPeriodIndexArithmetic, the CrystallineCohomology and PadicDifferentialEquations Part IIs of BS17, HW23, KMS22, Abe-18, Xu–Zhu, D'Addezio, Tsuzuki) are merged, not duplicated. Route order from briefs, item dependencies and stage edges: SemisimpleAlgebrasPartII and HodgeStructuresPartII → CartierFlows → RigidCompanions, with CR.1/CR.2 and GlobalGaloisDeformations below them. The only cycle is the one in finding 1. The review's in-place changes were checked (three titles), and they introduced no error.

Cross-extraction owners compared: HEUER-25 and GUO-REINECKE-24 (findings 3), ABE-18 (finding 4), DADDEZIO-23 (no companion or p-adic-Simpson item), LANDESMAN-LITT-24 and KLEVDAL-PATRIKIS-25 (cohomological rigidity and integrality, in the same HodgeStructuresPartII job, so merged), LIU-ZHU-17 (its HodgeStructuresPartII brief exports Higgs/parameter-connection algebra to CartierFlows; consistent), GROECHENIG-WYSS-ZIEGLER-20 and -20-B (curve Hitchin systems at ET.2b; not a substitute, as EG20 says), CESNAVICIUS-19 and CESNAVICIUS-SCHOLZE-24 (Brauer groups; route 2 coordinates with SF.2), and DELIGNE-80 (finding 5).

Both are routed to route 3, CrystallineCohomologyPartIICartierFlows. That roadmap is a Part II of CrystallineCohomology: the queue briefs it to start where CrystallineCohomology stops, and route 3's own brief imports 'CR.1 crystals/connections'. Item 015 in turn depends on 004 (Higgs bundles), which is in route 1, HodgeStructuresPartII, and route 1's brief imports 'generic connection/crystal carriers from CrystallineCohomology:CR.1'. So CR.1 would need its own successor, and a successor of CR.1's consumer. Two items are marked planned at CR.1 in a form CR.1 does not plan. HEUER-25, accepted, owns 'Theorem 4.4: the local correspondence (Faltings; Heuer)', the equivalence between small pro-étale vector bundles and small Higgs bundles on toric charts. It owns the global correspondence as well, both in PadicHodgeTheoryPartIIPadicSimpson (job DESIGN-PadicHodgeTheoryPartII). Its route-5 brief says outright that 'The p-adic Simpson correspondence itself stays in PadicHodgeTheory's Part II'. findings.claim: The ℓ-adic half of Proposition 7.4(2) has no item and no supplier. The proof compares the ℓ-adic and crystalline H¹ of End⁰ through their L-functions. On the ℓ-adic side it needs three things. (a) Weight zero of the irreducible lisse sheaf V_s̄ with finite-order determinant: Lafforgue's Proposition VII.7(i) on curves, extended to higher dimension by [EK, Corollary 4.5]. (b) Purity of H^i for a pure lisse sheaf on a smooth proper variety (Weil II). (c) The ℓ-adic L-function / trace formula ([De1, (5.2.3)]). Item 133 imports only the p-adic side, from RD.6. Item 113 is one missing item that names 'purity of weight zero and proper smooth cohomological weights' with no owner. Route 4's brief imports 'RD.6 weights' only. Yet (b) is planned at DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.7, and Lafforgue's correspondence with its purity conclusions at GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands:GS.6. The prerequisites entry lists Weil II and Lafforgue as papers 'the atlas does not yet cover' (PROTOCOL §16), which is not so for (b) and for Lafforgue on curves. The higher-dimensional weight-zero statement of [EK, Corollary 4.5] has no owner at all. Deligne's [De3, (1.3.1)], used in 7.4(1), is also uncited by any item: a lisse sheaf that is irreducible but not geometrically irreducible splits after a finite constant extension.
findings.evidence: Paper pp.149–150: 'as V_s̄ and F, thus a fortiori End⁰(V_s̄) and End⁰(F), have weight zero (see [Laf, Proposition VII.7 (i)], corrected in [EK, Corollary 4.5]), the dimension of H¹(X_s̄, End⁰(V_s̄)) over Q̄_ℓ and of H¹_crys(X_s̄, End⁰(F))⊗Q̄_p over Q̄_p are computed as the number of weight-1 eigenvalues counted with multiplicities in the L-function'. p.149: 'Since an irreducible ℓ-adic sheaf which is not geometrically irreducible splits over a finite base change s′→s (see e.g. [De3, formula (1.3.1)])'. research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/DeligneWeightsAndPurity.json, DWP.7: 'For X₀ smooth and F lisse of weights≥w … for smooth proper X the whole H^i is pure'. GlobalShtukasAndFunctionFieldLanglands.json, GS.6: 'State the bijection between cuspidal automorphic representations … and irreducible continuous n-dimensional ell-adic representations with finite-order determinant … Prove local factors, purity and multiplicity conclusions'. research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20.result.json: item 113 dependencies [109, 110, 133]; item 133 planned [RD.6] ('For the overconvergent F-isocrystals …'). findings.claim: A gap the extraction missed: the proof of Lemma 4.11 that σ is a bijection cites a lemma that does not give it. The printed proof reverses the construction: C(E_s^j) 'again is stable and rigid by Lemma 3.4'. But Lemma 3.4 concerns only the Frobenius twist w^*. The paper proves that C^{-1} preserves rigidity (Proposition 3.5), not that C does, and no result states it. Item 076 repeats the printed route: 'Show it is bijective using the corresponding inverse equivalences and the large-p rigidity assertion'. A design that follows it has to prove rigidity of C(E), which the source never supplies. A correct argument is short. C^{-1}∘w^* is fully faithful, so σ(i)=σ(j) forces V_s^i ≅ V_s^j. The V_s^i are pairwise non-isomorphic because Proposition 4.10(c) makes the spread sections give a bijection onto the rigid points of the special fibre (see also item 052's disjointness). So σ is an injective self-map of a finite set, hence bijective. The lemma is true, and this is a gap in its proof. arXiv v4 has the same text.
findings.evidence: Paper p.134, proof of Lemma 4.11: 'Clearly, we can reverse the argument: starting with (E_s^j, ∇_s^j), then C(E_s^j, ∇_s^j) again is stable and rigid by Lemma 3.4, and thus w^{−1*}C(E_s^j, ∇_s^j) as well.' Lemma 3.4 (p.125): 'a stable Higgs bundle (V,θ) on Z is rigid if and only if the stable Higgs bundle w^*(V,θ) is rigid, and a stable integrable connection (E,∇) is rigid if and only if … w^*(E,∇) is rigid.' Proposition 3.5 (p.126): 'the inverse Cartier transform C^{−1}(V′_s, θ′_s) is a stable rigid integrable connection'. arXiv 1707.00752v4, lines of Lemma 4.11: the same sentence. research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20.result.json: sourceIssues E1–E10 have no Lemma 4.11 entry.
findings.fix: Add PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20/E11: kind gap, affects 'the proof', locator 'Proof of Lemma 4.11, p.134'. Quote the sentence above. Correction: 'σ is injective because C^{−1}∘w^* is fully faithful and the (V_s^i,θ_s^i) are pairwise non-isomorphic by Proposition 4.10(c); an injective self-map of a finite set is bijective.' known 'new'; searched: arXiv versions, the author's publication list, Crossref. Restate item 076's proof route in the same way, with a dependency on 065 (Proposition 4.10) and on 052's disjointness.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry for the proof of Lemma 5.5) and item 092
findings.claim: A false step in the proof of Lemma 5.5 is not recorded. Having ι∘ϱ ≃ (ϱ̃⊗Frac R)⊗χ with χ of order dividing r, the proof concludes from Tr(ϱ(g)) = χ(g)Tr(ϱ̃(g)) that 'χ(g)=1'. That does not follow when ϱ ≅ ϱ⊗χ for a non-trivial χ. Take Γ = Q₈ and ϱ its 2-dimensional irreducible representation, whose character vanishes off ±1. Then ϱ⊗χ ≅ ϱ for each of the three non-trivial characters χ. The constant deformation ϱ̃ = ϱ satisfies the displayed relation with χ ≠ 1. The lemma survives. ϱ̃⊗Frac R ≅ ι∘ϱ⊗χ^{−1} is defined over K, so the classifying map Spec R → M_B sends the generic point to a closed point. The deformation is therefore constant, whether or not χ=1. The step is wrong; nothing downstream depends on it.
findings.evidence: Paper p.140: 'We conclude the proof by observing that ι∘ϱ ≃ ϱ̃⊗χ implies that Tr(ϱ(g)) = χ(g)Tr(ϱ̃(g)) for all g∈Γ. Thus, we have χ(g)=1.' arXiv v4: 'Thus we have χ(g) = 1.' Q₈ character table: the 2-dimensional character is 2, −2, 0, 0, 0 on the classes {1}, {−1}, {±i}, {±j}, {±k}, so its product with any linear character is itself.
findings.fix: Add E12: kind error, affects 'nothing', locator 'Proof of Lemma 5.5, p.140'. Correction: 'ϱ̃⊗Frac(R) ≃ ι∘ϱ⊗χ^{−1} is a constant family, so the deformation is trivial; χ=1 is neither needed nor true in general (Q₈)'. Have item 092's proof sketch conclude from constancy, not from χ=1.

(3) Lemma 5.9's proof defines ϱ_big 'of π₁(C_Q̄p)', where the curve C has no role; it should be π₁(X_Q̄p). (4) The proof of Lemma 5.11 is lettered one step behind. findings.claim: The ring-level case that the proof of Theorem 2.17 actually uses is in Mathlib, and neither item cites it. The proof splits the Azumaya algebra as M_{p^d}(O) and uses that every M_{p^d}(O)-module is F^{⊕p^d} for a unique F. Mathlib has this as ModuleCat.matrixEquivalence, the equivalence ModuleCat R ≌ ModuleCat (Matrix ι ι R) with functor M ↦ (ι → M), and IsMoritaEquivalent.matrix. It also has IsAzumaya.matrix: a nontrivial matrix algebra is Azumaya. Item 023 is 'missing' and item 022 cites nothing, yet 023 states 'In the free rank-n case the underlying R-module is M^⊕n'. What remains missing is the sheaf/scheme version, the non-free P and the annihilator/support bookkeeping.
findings.evidence: Mathlib 082e2d3, Mathlib/RingTheory/Morita/Matrix.lean:187 'def ModuleCat.matrixEquivalence (i : ι) : ModuleCat R ≌ ModuleCat (Matrix ι ι R)', with functor ModuleCat.toMatrixModCat (line 41: 'obj M := ModuleCat.of (Matrix ι ι R) (ι → M)'). findings.claim: Two item-level inaccuracies. (1) Item 107 adds a hypothesis the example does not need: 'Require α⁻¹ integral as well to land in GL₁(O_Qbar)'. An algebraic integer α with |α|=1 is automatically a unit. Its complex conjugate ᾱ = α⁻¹ is a root of the same minimal polynomial over Q, hence an algebraic integer. So the paper's Example 6.3 is correct as printed, and the item should not suggest otherwise. (2) Item 132's locator reads '§4.17; §7'. There is no §4.17. The reference is to Corollary 4.17 (§4.2, pp.137–138), and to §7, pp.146–151.
findings.evidence: Paper p.146, Example 6.3: 'Let α∈Z̄∖μ_∞ be an algebraic integer which is not a root of unity such that |α|=1 … ϱ: π₁^top(Σ,x) → GL₁(Z̄)'. Argument: if P ∈ Z[x] is the monic minimal polynomial of α, then P(ᾱ) = conj(P(α)) = 0, and |α| = 1 gives ᾱ = α⁻¹; so α⁻¹ is a root of P and hence integral. Contents, p.103: §4 has subsections 4.1 and 4.2 only. research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20.result.json: item 107 statement, item 132 locator.
